answer.rationale: The binding constraint is the 14-day non-renewing expiry with the line at 94% and zero buffer, so the decision hinges on whether the low-cost vendor is a proven cutover or a cold start. memory_c2 is the linchpin: it records that moving primary supply to this vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, which would mean the mandate-meeting quote comes from an already-proven supplier rather than a new qualification, letting switch_primary_vendor satisfy the 18% cut without a true delivery-risk step-up. memory_c1 (incumbent stability) is the counterweight but is neutralized because the incumbent refused to reopen price and cannot meet the mandate. I am not choosing defer (no auto-renew implies lapse, unlike memory_c5's month-to-month non-critical case), negotiate (incumbent already refused), or add_second_source (does not by itself meet the mandate and leaves the expiring primary unbridged). Residual risk is real given no buffer, so the cutover should be staged with the incumbent held as short-term bridge where possible and completion of qualification confirmed next cycle; uncertainty is preserved pending the c2 archive check.
